selection_statement: Ten major institutions/networks with demonstrated title searches; not the ten objectively largest Indonesian libraries. Comparable current collection census missing and some very large institutions blocked. Continuation preserves the original ten selected institutions and adds UI Fasilkom as a separately scoped reserve; eleven observed successes in total.

marketplace.conclusion: Best breadth investments are new SLiMS and INLISLite adapters; no defensible current national LMS-share ranking established. Indonesia OneSearch is largest identified discovery partnership route, but OAI metadata does not provide live item state.
marketplace.largest_network_unlock: OneSearch 4,215 institutions (2025); partnership/API/metadata rights and live holdings require separate work.

limitations: No current comparable national collection census; titles/copies/digital records not summed.
All 10 are Java-based; infrastructure-constrained rural/outer-island coverage is not demonstrated by this pilot sample.
No product adapter execution, production registration, permissions outreach or integration was performed.
No access controls/TLS checks disabled or challenges solved; blocked catalogs retained as failures.
A query success establishes metadata retrieval, not take-home eligibility, live availability accuracy, or license permission.
Result counts can be mixed media, OR-token matches, stale or internally inconsistent; direct book records used as proof.

limits: New UGM official GET route is a homepage, not search results.
National Library had no new confirmed physical-catalog route; its restricted OPAC was not retried.
Historical, faculty-only, ambiguous-unit and live catalog-record counts cannot be ranked together.
continuation_summary.policy_method: Applied current app semantics: longest matching robots path, wildcard support, exact MyBookshelf product group then generic group; no first-match urllib.robotparser decisions used.
